'''Kuzhikalail M. Abraham''' is an American scientist, a recognized expert on [[lithium-ion]] and [[lithium-ion polymer]] batteries and is the inventor of the ultrahigh energy density [[lithium–air battery]].<ref name="google.com">{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=i4Ii5na93EIC&hl=en|title=K. M. Abraham – Google Scholar Citations|work=google.com}}</ref><ref name="doi: 10.1149/1.1836378">{{cite journal | doi = 10.1149/1.1836378 | volume=143 | title=A Polymer Electrolyte-Based Rechargeable Lithium/Oxygen Battery | journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society | pages=1–5| year=1996 | last1=Abraham | first1=K. M. | issue=1 | bibcode=1996JElS..143....1A | s2cid=96810495 }}</ref><ref name="US patent 5,510,209">US patent 5,510,209</ref> Abraham is the principal of E-KEM Sciences in Needham, Massachusetts and a professor at the Northeastern University Center for Renewable Energy Technologies,<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.northeastern.edu/research/centers/northeastern-university-center-for-renewable-energy-technology/ | title=Northeastern University Center for Renewable Energy Technology (NUCRET) | access-date=2015-07-23 | archive-date=2019-06-26 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626030844/http://www.northeastern.edu/research/centers/northeastern-university-center-for-renewable-energy-technology/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Northeastern University]], in Boston, Massachusetts.

==Early life==
Born in 1945 as the oldest of 9 children, Abraham received his primary and secondary school education in [[Ranny]], [[Kerala state|Kerala]], India. Abraham completed his bachelors and masters in Chemistry from [[St. Berchmans College]], [[Changanassery]] where he was the Thevercad gold medalist (awarded to the highest ranking student graduating with a B.Sc degree in Chemistry) in 1965.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sbcollege.ac.in|title=St. Berchmans College}}</ref> He received a national merit scholarship from the government of India for the M.Sc. degree studies from 1965 to 1967.

Abraham was awarded a Ph.D. in Chemistry in 1973 from [[Tufts University]], [[Medford, Massachusetts]]. Tufts recognized him in 2017 with its Most Outstanding Achievement and Services Award for an alumnus.

Abraham conducted post-doctoral research at [[Vanderbilt University]] and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1973 to 1975. He published his early research concerned with inorganic materials synthesis, [[NMR spectroscopy]], and materials analysis and characterization.

==Career==
Abraham is the author of more than 200 journal articles and fifteen patents on lithium and lithium-ion battery materials and performance, meeting proceedings and book chapters.<ref name="google.com"/> His opinions on Li-ion battery materials, performance and safety aspects are sought by news organizations such as [[Wired Magazine]] (after the Boeing 787 Li-ion battery Fires),<ref>[https://www.wired.com/2013/01/boeing-787-investigation-batteries/ Investigation Focuses on Combusting Batteries on Boeing 787 Dreamliner], Boeing's [https://www.wired.com/autopia/2013/boeing-787-battery-design-musk/Share Batteries Draw Criticism as Dreamliner Probe]{{dead link|date=November 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Paur |first=Jason |title=Investigators Pinpoint a Short Circuit Within a 787 Dreamliner Battery |language=en-US |magazine=Wired |url=https://www.wired.com/2013/02/ntsb-787-dreamliner/ |access-date=2023-08-11 |issn=1059-1028}}</ref> and the Chemical and Engineering News of the American Chemical Society<ref>"Dell Recall Lithium batteries", August 21, 2006 (http://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/cen-v084n034.p011a); "The Power of Pores", February 18, 2008  (http://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/cen-v086n007.p022); "Long-Life Lithium-Air Battery", June 18, 2012 (http://pubs.acs.org/toc/cenear/90/25)</ref> and [[Wall Street Journal]] (on the announcement of [[Tesla Motors]] to build its Li-ion battery Giga Factory.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Wohlsen |first=Marcus |title=Why Apple Could Win Big With Tesla's Giant New Battery Factory |language=en-US |magazine=Wired |url=https://www.wired.com/2014/02/teslas-giant-battery-factory-save-apple/ |access-date=2023-08-11 |issn=1059-1028}}</ref> He is also a professor in the chemistry department at [[Northeastern University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.northeastern.edu/chemistry/faculty/|title=Faculty|work=Chemistry & Chemical Biology|access-date=2015-07-23|archive-date=2014-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141105202902/http://www.northeastern.edu/chemistry/faculty/|url-status=dead}}</ref> His contributions to lithium and lithium-ion batteries have been recognized by the [[Electrochemical Society]] by awarding him the Battery Research Award for outstanding contributions to primary and secondary lithium batteries,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pg 61-76 |url=http://www.electrochem.org/dl/interface/sum/sum05/IF08-05_Pg61-76.pdf |website=www.electrochem.org}}</ref> and election as a Fellow of the Electrochemical Society.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.electrochem.org/awards/ecs/recipients/fellow_recipients.htm|title=ECS Fellows|work=electrochem.org}}</ref> In addition, the Electrochemical Society recognized KM's contributions to the society and to the advancement of battery technologies by hosting a podcast featuring his scientific career in its Master Series on the society website.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ecs.podbean.com/e/km-abraham-on-lithium-batteries/|title=K.M. Abraham on the Invention of Li-air and Other Lithium Batteries|access-date=2018-06-08|archive-date=2019-08-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831060330/https://ecs.podbean.com/e/km-abraham-on-lithium-batteries/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is also a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]. The International Battery Association (IBA) recognized Abraham in 2018 with the Yeager Award for his Distinguished and Pioneering Contributions to Rechargeable Lithium Batteries.

Abraham is listed in [[Marquis Who's Who]] in America, Who is Who in the World, Who is Who in Frontiers in Science and Technology and, Who is Who in Emerging Leaders in America.<ref>{{ISBN|9780837970356}}; {{ISBN|978-0-8379-1150-2}};  {{ISBN|9780837957012}}; {{ISBN|9781604624496}}</ref> Abraham was recognized by The Kerala Center, a social organization located in Elmont, New York<ref>{{cite web|url=http://keralacenterny.com/Awardee2011.html|title=THE KERALA CENTER – AWARDS 2011|access-date=2015-07-23|archive-date=2018-10-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012045628/http://keralacenterny.com/Awardee2011.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> with the Outstanding Achievement Award for Applied Science in 2011. In 2021, he was recognized with the New England Choice Awards in the category of Academia & Innovation.

Abraham served as chair of the Battery Division and a member of board of directors of the [[Electrochemical Society]] from 2006 to 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.electrochem.org/ecs/tia/batt/division_chairs/|title=Battery Division Chairs|work=electrochem.org}}</ref> He was previously vice chair, secretary and treasurer of the battery division of the Electrochemical Society from 2000 to 2006 and served as chair of its Battery Research Award Committee in 2009. Abraham was also chair, vice chair, secretary and treasurer of the Boston Local Section of the [[Electrochemical Society]] from 1983 to 1987.

He is a member of the [[American Chemical Society]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acs.org|title=American Chemical Society|work=acs.org}}</ref> [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], Sigma Xi9, and [[Electrochemical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.electrochem.org/|title=Welcome to ECS: The Electrochemical Society|work=electrochem.org}}</ref> He is also a member of board of governors of the Kerala Development and Innovation Council (K-DISC)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kdisc.kerala.gov.in/index.php/organisation|title=Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC)|access-date=2018-06-08|archive-date=2019-08-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831060332/http://kdisc.kerala.gov.in/index.php/organisation|url-status=dead}}</ref> in its inaugural organization formed in March 2018.

Abraham is a pioneer in the research and development of rechargeable lithium and lithium-ion batteries. His research to demonstrate a practical rechargeable lithium battery began in the late nineteen seventies when no such rechargeable batteries existed. He and his colleagues pursuant to the development of stable electrolytes to recharge the lithium electrode<ref>U.S. Patent 4,489,145</ref> demonstrated one of the first sealed high capacity rechargeable [[lithium battery]] exhibiting several hundred charge/discharge cycles, a feat not accomplished until that time.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1149/1.2127279 | volume=128 | issue=12 | title=Rechargeable Lithium/Vanadium Oxide Cells Utilizing 2Me-THF/LiAsF<sub>6</sub> | journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society | pages=2493–2501| year=1981 | last1=Abraham | first1=K. M. | bibcode=1981JElS..128.2493A }}</ref> This work was the forerunner to the commercially successful [[Li-ion batteries]]. Another contribution of Abraham and his colleagues involved the development of highly conductive gel polymer electrolytes and those supported on micro-porous polymer membranes.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1149/1.2086749 | volume=137 | issue=5 | title=Li+-Conductive Solid Polymer Electrolytes with Liquid-Like Conductivity | journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society | pages=1657–1658| year=1990 | last1=Abraham | first1=K. M. | bibcode=1990JElS..137.1657A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1149/1.2048517 | volume=142 | issue=3 | title=Polymer Electrolytes Reinforced by Celgard Membranes | journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society | pages=683–687| year=1995 | last1=Abraham | first1=K. M. | bibcode=1995JElS..142..683A }}</ref><ref>US patent 5, 219,679</ref> Today such separator-embedded gel polymer electrolytes are used to build the commercially successful lithium-ion polymer batteries. Other pioneering contributions of Abraham include rechargeable sodium battery chemical couples that operate at moderately high temperatures,<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1149/1.2115227 | volume=131 | issue=10 | title=Moderate Temperature Sodium Cells | journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society | pages=2211| year=1984 | last1=Abraham | first1=K. M. | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>US patent 4,452,777</ref> the very high energy density non-aqueous [[Lithium–sulfur battery|lithium-sulfur battery]],<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1149/1.2129079 | volume=126 | issue=4 | title=A Lithium/Dissolved Sulfur Battery with an Organic Electrolyte | journal=Journal of the Electrochemical Society | pages=523–527| year=1979 | last1=Rauh | first1=R. D. }}</ref> the ultrahigh energy density non-aqueous [[lithium-air battery]],<ref name="doi: 10.1149/1.1836378"/><ref name="US patent 5,510,209"/> and the fundamental principles underlying the concept of chemical over charge protection of rechargeable lithium and [[Li-ion]] batteries.<ref>US patents 4,857,423</ref><ref>US Patent 5,858,573</ref> The research and development of [[lithium-air]] batteries is pursued world-wide for portable power, electric vehicles and large scale energy storage. His unique background encompasses both the fundamental science and engineering development of advanced batteries.

In 2022 Dr. Abraham established an endowment fund at his alma mater, [[St. Berchmans College]], [[Changanassery]], [[Kerala]]. The fund was used to build a Smart Class room in the  chemistry department in honor of Kuzhikalayil Family, and for Scholarships to needy undergraduate students.
